ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Timestep-conditioned routing for a mixture-of-experts DiT
PROPOSAL: Condition the router of a DiT-B/2 mixture-of-experts model on the diffusion timestep embedding, so that the same patch can reach different experts at high and low noise. Use 8 experts with top-2 selection in alternate blocks, train on ImageNet 256 latents for 400000 steps with classifier-free guidance dropout, and report FID, Inception score, sample quality at 250 sampling steps and per-timestep expert load. Compare token-to-expert assignments at timesteps 100, 500 and 900 with a mutual-information measure.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-B/2 with matching activated parameters; the same mixture without timestep conditioning; a variant that assigns experts by timestep range only, as in earlier U-Net mixtures.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Timestep conditioning should lower FID against the unconditioned router and raise assignment mutual information with noise level. It could fail if noise level dominates routing and experts split by timestep instead of by content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router-entropy audit of token-choice mixtures in small DiT models
PROPOSAL: Train DiT-S/2 token-choice mixtures on ImageNet 256 latents with 4 to 32 experts, 3 seeds each, for 100000 steps, and log router entropy, expert load and pairwise similarity of expert outputs at regular checkpoints. Repeat each run with single and double expert selection and with 3 values of the balancing coefficient, then compute how routing entropy changes with the diffusion timestep. Report FID next to each entropy curve, and compare each run to its dense twin.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-S/2 at matching activated parameters; a random fixed router; a router with frozen weights after 10000 steps; report correlation of entropy with FID over all runs.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Entropy should rise with expert count while FID barely moves. It could fail if the runs are too short for routing statistics to stabilise, or if variation among seeds is wider than the shift in entropy from one expert count to the next.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Group-size study of patch pooling for routing in diffusion transformers
PROPOSAL: Study how the size of the patch group that a router sees changes expert behaviour. Train DiT-S/2 mixtures with 8 experts on ImageNet 256 latents for 100000 steps, forming groups of 1, 2, 4 and 8 patches along each side, with 3 seeds per size and 2 pooling operators (mean and strided convolution). Report FID, group purity against segmentation masks of 5000 validation images, and load balance for each resulting run, and plot purity against FID with a fitted trend line for each pooling operator.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-S/2; token-level top-2 routing; random pairing of patches at each group size; plot purity against FID for every run.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Purity should peak at an intermediate group size. It could fail if pooling operator and seed variation mask the effect of group size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Neighbourhood-aware routing that groups adjacent patches before expert selection
PROPOSAL: Route groups of adjacent latent patches jointly instead of single tokens: a lightweight convolution pools each 2 by 2 neighbourhood into a group descriptor, the router selects experts for the descriptor, and all patches in the group follow that choice. Train a DiT-L/2 mixture with 32 experts on ImageNet 512 latents for 1000000 steps with 3 seeds and report FID, expert-purity of groups measured against segmentation masks of 5000 validation images, and the load balance across experts.
CONTROLS: Token-level top-2 routing at matching activated parameters; groups of 4 by 4 patches; groups formed by random pairing of patches; a dense DiT-B/2.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Group routing should improve expert purity and FID relative to token-level routing at the 2 by 2 size. It could fail at object boundaries, where a group spans two semantic regions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orthogonality loss on expert outputs to enforce specialization
PROPOSAL: Add a loss that penalises overlap between the output subspaces of different experts, computed from the cosine similarity of expert outputs on the same batch of tokens, with weight 0.01. Train a DiT-S/2 mixture with 8 experts on ImageNet 256 latents at batch size 256 for 200000 steps, and report FID on 10000 samples, a specialization score based on the entropy of class labels among tokens routed to each expert, and expert output similarity during training.
CONTROLS: The same mixture without the loss; the loss applied to router logits instead of expert outputs; a dense DiT-S/2 at matching activated parameters.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Specialization score should rise and FID improve slightly over the plain mixture. It could fail if the loss pushes experts apart in output space without making them handle distinct content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Balancing-coefficient search for small diffusion-transformer mixtures
PROPOSAL: Search the auxiliary balancing coefficient for DiT-S/2 mixtures with 8 experts on ImageNet 256 latents. Try balancing coefficients on a logarithmic scale spanning three orders of magnitude, 3 gating temperatures and routing sparsity levels, train each configuration for 50000 steps with 3 seeds, and report FID, expert load imbalance and the fraction of dropped tokens. Re-train the best configurations for 200000 steps and report the same measures with a dense twin, plus a heat map of FID over coefficient and temperature.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-S/2; a mixture with a noisy gating baseline; report rank agreement between the short runs and the long runs.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: An intermediate coefficient should balance load without hurting FID. It could fail if short-run rankings disagree with long-run rankings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert-count study of small diffusion mixtures with and without a shared expert
PROPOSAL: Run a grid over expert counts from 4 to 48 on DiT-S/2 mixtures, each with and without one shared expert and with single and double expert selection, trained on ImageNet 256 latents for 100000 steps with 3 seeds. Report FID, expert utilisation and the class-label entropy per expert per run with the fraction of dropped tokens at each layer, and fit a power law of FID against total parameters per variant.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-S/2 at matching activated parameters; report seed spread per setting; compare fitted exponents between variants.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: FID should improve with expert count up to a point and flatten later. It could fail if seed spread swamps the differences between neighbouring counts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shared-plus-routed experts with growing expert count at matched activated parameters
PROPOSAL: Test whether specialization survives growth in the number of experts by pairing one always-on shared expert with routed experts, keeping activated parameters fixed while the routed pool grows from 8 up to 256 experts. Train DiT-L/2 mixtures on ImageNet 512 latents for 800000 steps with 3 seeds and report FID, expert utilisation, and the specialization score from class-label entropy per expert. Fit a power law of FID against total parameters.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-B/2; routed-only mixtures at the same expert counts; mixtures where the shared expert is replaced by an extra routed expert at the same activated size.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The shared expert should keep FID improving as the pool grows, while routed-only variants flatten. It could fail if utilisation collapses to a few experts at 64.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt-conditioned routing for a text-to-image mixture-of-experts DiT
PROPOSAL: Build a text-to-image DiT with 24 blocks where the router receives both the patch token and a pooled embedding of the prompt from a frozen T5 encoder, so that experts can specialise by visual concept as well as by position. Train on CC12M-style caption pairs at 256 resolution for 600000 steps with 16 experts and top-2 selection, and evaluate FID, CLIP score and GenEval on a 30000 prompt set. Report expert assignment maps for 40 prompts spanning animals, faces, text, landscapes and objects.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT with matching activated parameters; token-only routing; routing by prompt only; expert-choice routing from earlier work.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Prompt conditioning should raise GenEval compositional scores and give assignments aligned with concepts. It could fail if prompt-driven routing makes experts duplicate the cross-attention path.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Concept-routing probe for small text-to-image mixtures with prompt embeddings
PROPOSAL: Probe whether prompt embeddings help routing in small text-to-image DiTs. Train 6 mixtures with 8 experts on 256-resolution CC12M-style data for 100000 steps each, varying prompt pooling (mean, max, attention), the number of routed layers (6, 12, 24) and the temperature of the router, with 3 seeds. Evaluate FID, CLIP score and GenEval on a 10000 prompt set, plus assignment maps for 40 prompts, and compare each run against a dense baseline of equal activated size.
CONTROLS: Token-only routing; routing by prompt alone; random assignments; correlate CLIP score with assignment purity across runs.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Prompt pooling should help GenEval more than FID. It could fail if all pooling variants give the same results inside seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Band-energy profiling of latent tokens in diffusion transformers
PROPOSAL: Profile the Haar band energies of latent patches from ImageNet 256 encodings at 10 noise levels, cluster them with 4 to 32 groups, and measure how well each clustering predicts the expert chosen by routers trained in 6 DiT-S/2 mixtures with 8 experts. Train every mixture for 100000 steps with 3 seeds, and report mutual information between clusters and routing choices, FID, and spectra of generated samples for each run.
CONTROLS: Clusterings built on pixel colour instead of band energy; a randomly permuted cluster labelling; a dense DiT-S/2 at the same activated size.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Band-energy clusters should predict routing better than colour clusters. It could fail if routers separate tokens by position rather than by frequency content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frequency-aware routing using wavelet bands of latent patches
PROPOSAL: Compute a one-level Haar decomposition of each latent patch and feed the band energies into the router as added features, so that smooth patches and high-frequency patches can be sent to different experts. Train a DiT-L/2 mixture with 16 experts, top-2, on ImageNet 512 latents for 1000000 steps with 3 seeds. Report FID on 50000 samples, a per-expert frequency profile and a high-frequency fidelity metric based on spectra of generated samples.
CONTROLS: The same mixture without frequency features; frequency features fed into the experts instead of the router; a dense DiT-B/2 with matching activated parameters.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Experts should divide into smooth-region and texture-region groups, improving high-frequency fidelity. It could fail if latent patches carry too little frequency structure to separate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing token-choice, expert-choice and batch-level routing with specialization metrics
PROPOSAL: Implement token-choice, expert-choice and batch-level global routing in one DiT-B/2 codebase and train each with 16 experts at the same number of activated parameters on ImageNet 256 latents for 400000 steps. Report FID, expert utilisation, class-label entropy per expert and the stability of assignments between checkpoints 50000 steps apart, along with a dense DiT-B/2. Add a version of each router with a learned token embedding that depends on spatial position.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-B/2 at matching activated parameters; each router with position embeddings removed; each router with random assignments in the final blocks.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Expert-choice routing should give the highest utilisation, while specialization scores stay close for all three. It could fail if training length matters more than router type.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Router-type comparison on small diffusion mixtures over capacity factors
PROPOSAL: Compare token-choice, expert-choice and batch-level routers on DiT-S/2 mixtures with 8 experts and a few capacity factors, trained for 100000 steps on ImageNet 256 latents with 3 seeds. Report FID, expert utilisation, class-label entropy per expert and assignment stability at regular intervals, and train the winners again with 16 experts for 200000 steps to check that rankings persist, with a table of the final ranks of all routers.
CONTROLS: A dense DiT-S/2; each router with position embeddings removed; report rank agreement between the two scales.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Rankings between routers should hold at both scales, with expert-choice routing leading on utilisation. It could fail if the capacity factor changes which router wins, or if training length matters more than the router type.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Centroid-initialisation study for routers in upcycled diffusion mixtures
PROPOSAL: Study router initialisation when a dense DiT-S/2 is upcycled into a mixture. Gather block-input tokens from 50000 to 200000 ImageNet latents, derive centroids with 8 to 32 clusters in 4 different layers, and initialise routers from them; continue training each resulting mixture for 20000 steps with 3 seeds. Report FID, utilisation and class-label entropy per expert, and the similarity of copied experts over training. Plot utilisation against step for each layer and report the layer with the steadiest assignments.
CONTROLS: A random router; a class-conditional router; the dense model continued for equal steps; report which layer matters most.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Centroids from more tokens should give steadier utilisation. It could fail if initialisation is forgotten within a few thousand steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Upcycling a dense DiT-B/2 into a mixture with cluster-initialised routing
PROPOSAL: Convert a trained dense DiT-L/2 into a mixture by copying each feed-forward block into 32 experts and initialising the router from k-means centroids of the block's input tokens gathered on 500000 ImageNet latents. Continue training for 600000 steps at a reduced learning rate with 3 seeds and report FID against the dense model trained for the same number of steps, expert utilisation and a specialization score from class-label entropy per expert.
CONTROLS: Upcycling with a random router; upcycling with a router initialised from class-conditional means; the dense model continued for the same steps with matching activated parameters.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Cluster initialisation should speed up specialization and give lower FID than random routing. It could fail if copied experts stay too similar to diverge within the continued training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Linear probes on a small DiT to find which token properties drive routing
PROPOSAL: Train a DiT-S/2 mixture with 8 experts on ImageNet 256 latents for 60000 steps with 3 seeds, then fit linear probes that predict each token's chosen expert from 5 candidate properties: grid position, noise level, local gradient energy, class label and the object-versus-background mask. Report probe accuracy for each property alone and in pairs, and a variance decomposition of routing decisions, on 20000 held-out tokens per layer.
CONTROLS: A probe on shuffled expert labels; a probe on a router frozen at initialisation; the same analysis on a dense model with a k-nearest-neighbour partition of tokens.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Position and noise level should explain most routing, class and object mask little. It could fail if the short training leaves the router near initialisation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probe-suite of token properties on routers of small diffusion mixtures
PROPOSAL: Fit probes that predict the chosen expert from a dozen token properties on DiT-S/2 mixtures with 8 experts, trained for 60000 steps with 3 seeds on ImageNet 256 latents. Use linear, two-layer and gradient-boosted probes on tokens from all layers at regular checkpoints, report accuracy per property and per layer, and compare the three probe families on 20000 held-out tokens, plotting probe accuracy against layer for each property with confidence intervals over seeds.
CONTROLS: Probes on shuffled labels; probes on a frozen random router; report the agreement of property rankings between seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Property rankings should agree between seeds and between probe families. It could fail if gradient-boosted probes overfit and reorder the properties.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-by-layer separability profile of visual and language tokens
PROPOSAL: Compute silhouette, nearest-neighbour label agreement and effective rank for activations at all 12 layers of a DiT-B/2 on 10000 ImageNet latents at 8 timesteps, and for a 125M-parameter language model on 10000 sentences, with 5 token subsample sizes and 3 random draws of tokens. Relate each statistic to the expert utilisation of mixtures trained on each modality, and plot the profiles layer by layer, with bootstrap intervals over tokens for each statistic and a short table of the layers with the biggest gap.
CONTROLS: A randomly initialised network of the same shape; pixel patches without a network; report the spread over random draws.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Separability should differ most in the middle layers. It could fail if profiles are flat across layers and subsample sizes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distinguishability of visual and language tokens by clustering quality
PROPOSAL: Quantify how separable DiT patch tokens are compared with language tokens. Take block-8 activations of a DiT-B/2 on 10000 ImageNet latents at timesteps 200 and 800, and token activations from a 125M-parameter language model on 10000 sentences, then measure silhouette, nearest-neighbour label agreement and effective rank for matched token counts. Relate these statistics to the expert utilisation of a mixture trained on each modality for 200000 steps with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Activations from a randomly initialised network of the same shape; matched token counts subsampled at 5 sizes; the same statistics on pixel patches without a network.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Visual tokens should show lower silhouette and effective rank than language tokens, especially at high noise. It could fail if the comparison depends mostly on layer choice.
